title: Rusty crust made Mars warm and wet | New Scientist
description: It's unclear how and why Mars once became warm enough to allow water to flow on its surface, but a new idea suggests it comes down to rust below the surface
author: Bas den Hond

title: Binance: How did the biggest crypto heist in history just happen? | New Scientist
description: Billions of dollars' worth of cryptocurrency have been stolen in just a matter of minutes. Researchers are already unpicking what went wrong
author: Chris Stokel-Walker

title: Scientists confirm fruit and vegetable skin really is good for you | New Scientist
description: Parts of plants that are usually wasted, from kiwi skin to squash seeds, contain more fibre than the parts of the plant we do eat
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Plant biology provides inspiration for PFAS replacement | New Scientist
description: Forever chemicals are renowned for their durability and their non-stick properties, but they persist for years in the environment. An alternative inspired by plants doesn't have the same problem
author: Victoria Atkinson

title: Birds can get jet lag on long, fast flights and then fly off course | New Scientist
description: On fast flights across the Atlantic, the body clocks of Manx shearwaters get out of sync with local time, leading them to veer away from the most direct flight path
author: Michael Le Page

title: Inhaling CO2 may rescue nerves’ ability to regrow | New Scientist
description: Breathing out after birth switches off the ability of tissues to regenerate, a study in mice suggests. But the pathway seems to be reversible
author: Jo Marchant
